themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 6 THIS WEEK—a 4700% spike from the 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in Central Harlem's public spaces.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 17.76)
Represents 4700% spike—highest statistical deviation in district data
Timing aligns with recent political activity (mayoral 100-day rally on 2026-04-13)
reporting_angles: Investigate what is being posted and who is responsible—political campaign material, illegal ads, or other signage?
Interview 311 data analysts and Parks Enforcement Patrol about enforcement capacity and posting patterns in recent weeks

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Spike This Week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, an 833% increase from the 0.8 weekly baseline, pointing to a sudden deterioration in public space maintenance or a localized tagging campaign.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.54)
Clusters with illegal posting spike, suggesting coordinated public-space degradation
reporting_angles: Document specific locations and tags—are they territorial, political, or random?
Interview Parks Department about removal timelines and resource allocation for Harlem

themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Enforcement Crackdown
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints surged 900% to 5 last week (vs. 0.5 weekly average), suggesting either increased street vending or a city enforcement operation targeting informal economy activity in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.2)
Timing precedes mayoral 100-day 'pothole politics' rally (2026-04-13) with quality-of-life focus
reporting_angles: Speak with street vendors in major commercial corridors (125th St, Frederick Douglass Blvd) about enforcement interactions
Verify if this reflects a city-wide vendor crackdown or Harlem-specific enforcement operation

themes_detail.label: Missed Garbage Collection Problem
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints jumped 363% to 11 last week (vs. 2.4 weekly average), indicating sanitation service reliability issues that compound existing unsanitary condition complaints (1,285 over 90 days).
evidence: 11 missed collection complaints last week vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 2.84)
363% spike in missed pickups follows trend of 1,285 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days
Sanitation is top recurring budget request (DEP capital/expense), indicating chronic under-resourcing
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department about staffing, truck maintenance, or route changes in Central Harlem
Document impact on block conditions and resident health—photograph affected streets

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Crisis (Chronic)
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints total 7,256 over 90 days—by far the largest complaint category—yet do not show a NEW spike this week, indicating a chronic, unresolved housing code enforcement problem requiring investigation despite lacking recent acceleration.
evidence: 7,256 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days—12x higher than next-largest category (3,320 noise complaints)
Chronic pattern reflects systemic housing code enforcement gap despite 'Upgrade existing facilities for the homeless' repeated budget request
No statistical spike THIS WEEK suggests institutionalized non-compliance rather than emergency
reporting_angles: Investigate which buildings are chronic repeaters—map HPD violation history and enforcement delays
Interview tenants in affected buildings about winter hardship and landlord accountability
